root_cause.text: The UDP receive cleanup path in `skb_consume_udp()` incorrectly assumed consumed UDP skbs never had an attached destructor, so after commit `6471658dc66c` it called `skb_attempt_defer_free()` on non-shared skbs without first orphaning skbs whose ownership/destructor had been set by the skmsg path via `skb_set_owner_sk_safe()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `skb_orphan(skb);` immediately before `skb_attempt_defer_free(skb);` in `net/ipv4/udp.c`, and the commit/CVE explicitly state that while the standard UDP path does not use `skb->destructor`, the skmsg layer does from `udp_read_skb()`, which triggers `DEBUG_NET_WARN_ON_ONCE(skb->destructor)` in `skb_attempt_defer_free()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Orphan unshared UDP sk_buffs before deferred free so socket ownership state is properly cleared during skb consumption.
intent_record.what: A call to skb_orphan(skb) was added inside skb_consume_udp() in the branch where !skb_shared(skb) is true, immediately before skb_attempt_defer_free(skb) and the return.
intent_record.how: At runtime, unshared UDP sk_buffs now have their ownership association cleared before deferred freeing is attempted, ensuring any socket-related destructor or accounting state is detached prior to release and preventing incorrect retention of owner state during skb cleanup.

This conditional identifies the non-shared skb path where the code incorrectly assumed no destructor/owner was attached, leading to the unsafe direct call to deferred free.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is the direct vulnerable operation: in the unshared UDP skb consume path it defers freeing the skb without first orphaning it, so any socket ownership/destructor previously attached via skb_set_owner_sk_safe() remains uncleared, matching the described root cause.

This conditional gates the specific non-shared skb path where the buggy assumption was made that consumed UDP skbs had no attached destructor. It defines the vulnerable control-flow region that leads to the unsafe deferred free call.

Author: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 16 16:09:51 2025 +0000

    udp: use skb_attempt_defer_free()
    
    Move skb freeing from udp recvmsg() path to the cpu
    which allocated/received it, as TCP did in linux-5.17.
    
    This increases max thoughput by 20% to 30%, depending
    on number of BH producers.
    
    Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
    Acked-by: Willem de Bruijn <willemb@google.com>

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the exact logic added to `skb_consume_udp()` and it is sufficient to evaluate the stated root cause. The new fast path is: `if (!skb_shared(skb)) { if (unlikely(udp_skb_has_head_state(skb))) skb_release_head_state(skb); skb_attempt_defer_free(skb); return; }`. This means non-shared UDP skbs are now passed to `skb_attempt_defer_free()` directly. The root cause says the bug is that this path assumed consumed UDP skbs never had an attached destructor and therefore failed to orphan skbs whose ownership/destructor had been set via `skb_set_owner_sk_safe()`. In the shown code, there is no orphaning step such as `skb_orphan()` before `skb_attempt_defer_free(skb)`. Releasing head state with `skb_release_head_state(skb)` is not the same as orphaning an skb with an attached owner/destructor from the skmsg path. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not yet present.
